subject.title: improve(gateway): tunable control-plane write rate limit, default unchanged

question: Should an authenticated gateway admin be allowed to hot-raise the gateway-global control-plane limiter that constrains its own subsequent admin writes?
rationale: The implementation is internally coherent, but tests cannot decide whether the limiter is operational pacing that trusted admins may tune or a defense-in-depth boundary that constrained callers must not modify.

options.title: Accept the bounded global knob
options.body: Keep the unchanged default, 600-request ceiling, per-identity buckets, warnings, and audit trail, then merge after conflict resolution and focused validation.

options.title: Narrow quota administration
options.body: Expose higher quotas only through a host-local, startup-only, or separately privileged path that ordinary constrained admin RPCs cannot change.

options.title: Keep the fixed protection
options.body: Decline the new config contract and require supported batching or distribution across independent gateways for burst automation.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded global knob
recommendation.body: Keep the unchanged default, 600-request ceiling, per-identity buckets, warnings, and audit trail, then merge after conflict resolution and focused validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their commits introduced and hardened the current protection, providing the strongest available ownership signal for defining its permanent trust boundary.
